run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Yes — the recent logs for the traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b contain one error-level record. Pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l wrote, at 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z, the JSON line {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}; it is the only error-level line and the only line carrying a 5xx status for these pods in the last hour (1 of 51 lines on that pod; the other two pods logged 50 info lines each). Otherwise the workload looks healthy at the object level: Deployment traffic-manager has 3/3 ready replicas at revision 1, was created 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z by kubectl-client-side-apply (nginx:latest, resources {}), its ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 was scaled 0→3, and all three pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance; their container logs show only normal nginx startup notices and HTTP 2xx request lines. All events naming traffic-manager are Normal; the only Warning events in the window are unrelated Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint 'already exists' events for app-219/mariadb, app-100a/loki, app-101/loki and app-102/loki (a different namespace from app-102b). The cause of the single error line is unresolved: Prometheus was unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on every attempt, so neither pod/container memory usage nor error-rate series nor alert rules could be checked, and the node reported MemoryPressure=False ('kubelet has sufficient memory available'). No fault-injecting configuration was found in the namespace (the only ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt). The reported 501 and the claimed memory condition are therefore a single observed log line whose origin and user impact are unverified.

claims.text: Deployment traffic-manager in namespace app-102b is at revision 1, created 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z by manager kubectl-client-side-apply, with replicas 3, image nginx:latest, container name nginx, port 80, and an empty resources block (resources: {}); its status shows 3 replicas, 3 readyReplicas, 3 availableReplicas.

Pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l, traffic-manager-585c5579f6-f2p6c and traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nm5h6 are all phase Running and Ready, owned by ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6, started 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z, with container nginx ready, restartCount 0 and an empty lastState.

The only error-level log record found for these pods is on traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l at 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z: {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}, with labels namespace=app-102b, pod=traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l, container=nginx, app=nginx, job=nginx.

Log line counts in the hour ending 2026-11-23T19:04:33Z were: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l 50 detected_level=info and 1 detected_level=error; pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-f2p6c 50 info and 0 error; pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nm5h6 50 info and 0 error. A namespace-wide level count over the same hour returned only these three pods, i.e. only the traffic-manager workload logged in app-102b in that hour.

Counting log lines matching a 5xx "status" field over the hour ending 2026-11-23T19:04:33Z returned exactly one series (pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l, value 1); no 5xx-status lines were counted for pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-f2p6c or traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nm5h6.

The application log stream of the traffic-manager pods in app-102b (151 lines shown for the whole authorized window, all timestamped 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z) consists of INFO 'HTTP request completed' records on paths /health, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/products and /api/v1/inventory with status values 200, 201 and 204 and response_time_ms between 50 and 198, plus the single ERROR 'Memory alert' record.

Container stdout of all three pods covers only their startup: 23 lines each from the current nginx instance between 2026-11-23T19:04:25Z and 19:04:26Z containing docker-entrypoint/nginx notices ('Configuration complete; ready for start up', 'start worker processes') and no error text; the previous container instance was reported as not found for each pod, and restartCount is 0.

All events naming traffic-manager objects in namespace app-102b are type Normal: Deployment 'Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3' (ScalingReplicaSet, 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z), three ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate events, and Pod Scheduled/Pulling/Pulled/Created/Started events between 19:04:24Z and 19:04:26Z. No Warning event names traffic-manager.

The only Warning events in the whole authorized window are four Endpoints events with reason FailedToCreateEndpoint and message 'Failed to create endpoint for service <ns>/<svc>: endpoints "<svc>" already exists': app-219/mariadb at 2026-11-23T18:27:05Z, app-100a/loki at 18:29:58Z, app-101/loki at 18:39:56Z and app-102/loki at 18:50:09Z; these involve Endpoints objects, not the traffic-manager workload in app-102b.
The only ConfigMap in namespace app-102b is kube-root-ca.crt (key ca.crt, created 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z); the traffic-manager Deployment defines no envFrom, env, volumes or configMap references.

Searching Loki cluster-wide for the text 'Memory alert' under job="nginx" over the authorized window returned exactly this one line on app-102b/traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l at 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane (the node all three pods are scheduled on) reports MemoryPressure status False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory and message 'kubelet has sufficient memory available', and reports 32859952Ki allocatable memory — so no node-level memory pressure is visible that would corroborate a cluster-wide memory shortage.

The error is confined to one pod and one line: pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-f2p6c and traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nm5h6 produced 50 info lines each and no error-level or 5xx-status lines in the same hour, and the observed request-status values across the workload were 200/201/204.

An application-level memory condition affected traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l: the ERROR record itself states 'Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory' and returns status 501. This remains a hypothesis — there is no memory-usage series (Prometheus unreachable), the container declares no resource requests (resources: {}), the node reports sufficient memory, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/restart evidence exists on any of the three pods. What the '90%' refers to and whether real memory pressure existed is unverified.

The single ERROR line with status 501 represents a request that failed on the pod that logged it (traffic-manager-585c5579f6-bnf7l), but no client-side or server-side metric (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_* series) could be read in this run, so neither the rate of such failures nor downstream/customer impact is established; one logged 501 is not a measured error rate.

A fault-injection setting in an app-102b ConfigMap or in the Deployment's environment did not cause the error: the namespace's only ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt (a CA bundle), and the Deployment's pod template contains no env, envFrom, volume or configMap reference.

Treat the Deployment rollout/scale-up at 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z (revision 1, ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 created, scaled 0→3) as a lifecycle event rather than a fault: no pod shows Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, a restart or a recreated previous container, and every pod-level event is Normal. If the memory alert matters, verify container memory working-set versus any configured request/limit and the alert rule that emitted it once Prometheus is reachable, and consider that the container currently declares no resources at all (resources: {}).

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this run: get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules and execute_prometheus_instant_query each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so container/pod memory usage series, HTTP/server error-rate series (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_*), traces_span_metrics_calls_total and any alerting rule behind the 'Memory requests above 90%' wording could not be checked; those signals are unknown, not zero.

What the '90%' in the ERROR record refers to, and whether any real memory pressure existed at 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z, is unverified — the container declares no memory request or limit and the node reports MemoryPressure=False.

The traffic-manager workload is only ~10 seconds old at the sampled time (Deployment/ReplicaSet/pods created 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z, all Loki lines timestamped 19:04:26Z), so there is no earlier baseline for its log volume, latency or error rate and nothing can be said about its behaviour before that instant.

fetch_pod_logs read only the current container instance (23 startup lines per pod) and reported no previous instance; the ERROR record is visible only in Loki, so whether the container wrote further error lines that Loki did not retain or that fall outside the sampled window is unknown.

Who or what created the traffic-manager Deployment at 19:04:24Z (kubectl client-side apply, revision 1) is not established; the Change History integration is not available in this run, so the trigger for the scale-up from 0 to 3 is unknown.
Whether any client actually received the logged 501, and whether anything downstream of traffic-manager was affected, is unverified; no caller-side evidence was collected.
next_steps: When Prometheus is reachable, check container memory working set versus requests/limits for pods of Deployment traffic-manager in app-102b, plus the alerting rule whose expression produces 'Memory requests above 90%', around 2026-11-23T19:04:26Z.

Look at the server-side request metrics (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count by status, or the traces_span_metrics_calls_total series for the nginx service) to size how often 501 responses occurred and whether they continued after the sampled second.

Confirm with the owner of the kubectl-client-side-apply that created Deployment traffic-manager (app-102b) at 2026-11-23T19:04:24Z whether the scale-up from 0 to 3 was an intentional rollout, and whether memory requests should be added to the container spec.

If the ERROR line must be reproduced, capture the pod's full log history and the request_id 'req-a]8f2c1d4' at the source, since the stored record is a single line and cannot be corroborated from the pod's own stdout read in this run.
